subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers cut a stable package/parity release for the affected `v2026.6.11` latest dist now, or wait for the next stable train while keeping this issue open?
rationale: The source fix is present on current main, but resolving this issue requires release ownership because npm latest and the latest GitHub stable release still point to the affected package.

options.title: Publish stable parity fix
options.body: Cut a stable release or repack that contains the current session-store dist output and verify the npm tarball before closing this issue.

options.title: Hold for next stable train
options.body: Keep this issue open and clearly treat `v2026.6.11` as affected until the next stable package is published.

options.title: Split channel retries only
options.body: Let channel-specific retry issues proceed separately, but do not use them as closure for this package parity tracker.

recommendation.title: Publish stable parity fix
recommendation.body: Cut a stable release or repack that contains the current session-store dist output and verify the npm tarball before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: This is now a release/package parity decision, and this person is tied to the latest stable release commit in the inspected history.
